newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Reps back income tax rebate plan on neighbors.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Reps back income tax rebate plan on neighbors.

text.p: The Illinois House has advanced a plan to recoup up to $55 million of personal income taxes from residents of neighboring states who commute across the Wisconsin and Indiana borders, a legislative aide said Monday.
The house approved the measure proposed by state Revenue Director Kenneth Zehnder on Friday and returned it to the senate for consideration, the aide said.

Under the legislation first introduced by Rep. Glenn Bradford, D-Glen Carbon, Wisconsin and Indiana would have the option of rebating the taxes they get from their residents who work in Illinois or informing them that they must begin paying Illinois income taxes in 1998.

Illinois has had reciprocal tax arrangements with Indiana and Wisconsin since the 1970s that allow residents to file a single income tax form in their home state on the assumption that there are an equal number of commuters crossing the borders.
Wisconsin paid Minnesota a $31.8 miillion rebate in 1996 for workers who live in western Wisconsin, but work across the St. Croix River in Minnesota, the Chicago Sun-Times reported Friday.

The Bradford proposal had been introduced as a bill that did not advance earlier in the session. Rep. Andrea Moore, R-Libertyville, picked it up as an amendment in the house and Sen. William Peterson, R-Prairie View, has signed on as the senate sponsor.
